brands.d: North Vancouver technical apparel maker (Rock Solid 1989, renamed 1991) known for Gore-Tex shells and down parkas; owned by Amer Sports.
Ventura outdoor clothing company founded by Yvon Chouinard in 1973; fleece pioneer with Malden Mills and 1% for the Planet since 1985.
Massimo Osti's Italian label (Chester Perry until 1978) known for military-inspired outerwear, garment dyeing and the 1988 Goggle Jacket.
Folding nylon windbreaker brand invented in northern France by Léon-Claude Duhamel in 1965, relaunched from Turin after 2004; name became generic.
Rosenheim maker of the rubberised Kleppermantel raincoat (1920, Johann Klepper) and folding kayaks; the coat's original form is no longer produced.
Newcastle-founded outdoor brand (Lockey and Davison), early European Gore-Tex user from 1977; Extrem range from 1986.
Founded in Monestier-de-Clermont by René Ramillon and André Vincent; relaunched as a Milan luxury house by Remo Ruffini from 2003; owns Stone Island.
Fast Retailing's casual-wear chain, born in Hiroshima in 1984; known for Heattech and Ultra Light Down.
Sheffield climbing-clothing maker founded by Rab Carrington in 1981, owned by Equip; known for down jackets and sleeping bags.
Massimo Osti's Ravarino label of 1982, named after Conrad; fabric research, garment dyeing and the compass badge; owned by Moncler since 2020.
Örnsköldsvik outdoor brand founded by Åke Nordin; Greenland Jacket and G-1000 fabric from 1968; Fenix Outdoor subsidiary.
Aosta label of 1987, first for waxed-canvas bags; Skidoo anorak 1990 and Rainforest 1995; VF subsidiary since 2004.
Beaverton sportswear giant whose All Conditions Gear outdoor line debuted in 1989.
Family-owned New York maker of the Perfecto motorcycle jacket, still largely made in the US.
Portland outdoor company founded 1938 by Paul Lamfrom, grown on breathable waterproof jackets with interchangeable liners.
Seon ropemaker of 1862 turned alpine clothing and equipment brand.
Massachusetts mill that developed polar fleece in 1979 and Synchilla with Patagonia; trades as Polartec.
